navigable-map-concept.title: Navigate ordered map keys with NavigableMap
navigable-map-concept.short: Find nearest keys above or below a target
navigable-map-concept.summary: NavigableMap extends sorted maps with operations such as floorEntry, ceilingEntry, lowerEntry, and higherEntry.
navigable-map-concept.why: It makes nearest-key and range-oriented lookups explicit without manually scanning a sorted collection.
navigable-map-concept.tips: TreeMap is the common implementation; define a comparator whose ordering remains consistent with the map's intended key semantics.

scoped-value-concept.title: Share immutable context with ScopedValue
scoped-value-concept.short: Bind context for a bounded dynamic scope
scoped-value-concept.summary: ScopedValue provides a controlled way to make immutable context available to callees during a bounded operation.
scoped-value-concept.why: It avoids passing context through every intermediate method and is designed to work well with modern Java concurrency.
scoped-value-concept.tips: Use scoped values for immutable contextual data, not as general mutable thread-local storage.

map-entry-comparing-by-value.title: Sort map entries by value
map-entry-comparing-by-value.summary: Map.Entry.comparingByValue creates a comparator that orders entries by their values.
map-entry-comparing-by-value.why: The standard comparator avoids repeating a lambda for a common entry-sorting operation.
map-entry-comparing-by-value.tips: Use the overload accepting a Comparator when values need a custom ordering.

files-probe-content-type.title: Probe a file content type
files-probe-content-type.short: Ask the installed file type detector for a media type
files-probe-content-type.summary: Files.probeContentType attempts to determine a file's content type and returns a media-type string or null when it cannot determine one.
files-probe-content-type.why: It provides a standard hook into platform and installed file type detectors instead of hard-coding only filename extensions.
files-probe-content-type.tips: Detection is implementation-dependent, so treat a null or unexpected result as a normal possibility.

buffer-overflow-exception.title: BufferOverflowException
buffer-overflow-exception.short: Do not write more data than the buffer has remaining space
buffer-overflow-exception.summary: BufferOverflowException is thrown when a relative put operation needs more remaining buffer space than is available.
buffer-overflow-exception.why: NIO buffers track a position and limit, and writes must fit between the current position and limit.
buffer-overflow-exception.tips: Check remaining(), size the buffer appropriately, or flush/compact a staged buffer before writing more data.

buffer-underflow-exception.title: BufferUnderflowException
buffer-underflow-exception.short: Do not read more data than remains in the buffer
buffer-underflow-exception.summary: BufferUnderflowException is thrown when a relative get operation needs more remaining data than the buffer contains.
buffer-underflow-exception.why: Reading a multi-byte value requires enough bytes between the current position and limit.
buffer-underflow-exception.tips: After writing before reading, use flip when appropriate and check remaining() when input may be incomplete.

record-canonical-constructor-access-erro.title: Record canonical constructor access
record-canonical-constructor-access-erro.short: Do not make the canonical constructor less accessible than the record
record-canonical-constructor-access-erro.summary: A record's canonical constructor cannot have more restrictive access than the record itself.
record-canonical-constructor-access-erro.why: The canonical constructor is the standard construction path corresponding to the record header, so its accessibility must preserve the record's API contract.
record-canonical-constructor-access-erro.tips: Match the constructor access to the record declaration and use validation inside the constructor rather than hiding it.

enum-constructor-public-error.title: Enum constructors cannot be public or protected
enum-constructor-public-error.short: Keep enum construction internal to the enum declaration
enum-constructor-public-error.summary: An enum constructor cannot be declared public or protected because enum instances are the declared constants, not caller-created objects.
enum-constructor-public-error.why: Java controls enum instance creation so the finite set of constants cannot be extended by ordinary constructor calls.
enum-constructor-public-error.tips: Use a package-private or private constructor syntax and pass constructor arguments from the enum constants.

unchecked-overriding-return-warning.title: Unchecked overriding return warning
unchecked-overriding-return-warning.short: Preserve generic return types when overriding legacy declarations
unchecked-overriding-return-warning.summary: An override involving raw and parameterized return types can require an unchecked conversion and produce a compiler warning.
unchecked-overriding-return-warning.why: Raw types erase generic guarantees that the overriding contract expects to preserve.
unchecked-overriding-return-warning.tips: Parameterize the overriding method consistently and isolate unavoidable legacy raw APIs at a narrow boundary.

stream-peek-side-effect-trap.title: Do not rely on Stream.peek for required side effects
stream-peek-side-effect-trap.short: peek is mainly for observing a pipeline, not business logic
stream-peek-side-effect-trap.summary: Stream implementations may optimize operations so peek actions are not a reliable place for required program behavior.
stream-peek-side-effect-trap.why: peek is an intermediate operation intended mainly for debugging and observation, and terminal-operation optimizations can avoid traversing elements in some pipelines.
stream-peek-side-effect-trap.tips: Put required work in explicit transformations or terminal processing and keep peek observational.
